dedupe_keys.name: pipeline agent decision support for natural gas pipelines with pipeline bench

description: Pipeline-Agent is a decision support system for operating natural gas transmission pipelines that uses a large language model only to plan and explain, while all safety-critical computations run in deterministic tools. It was published in 2026 in the Journal of Pipeline Science and Engineering by Liyu Zhang, Dou Huang, Weichao Yu, Weiyao Yang, Defan Feng and Hongbin Xie of Peking University and the Southern University of Science and Technology. The system aligns geographic information, network topology and time-indexed operational measurements into one spatiotemporal schema, creates an explicit plan, executes sandboxed tools and returns a verifiable package with intermediate artefacts and logs. The authors also introduce Pipeline-Bench, 80 task templates in eight categories, on which the agent scored 2.24 times the best baseline and 2.56 times direct generation by GPT-5.2. Coverage: gas transmission networks; the operational data used are not public. Access: open-access article; public code was not confirmed. Licence and cost: the article is CC BY 4.0, free. Caveats: a new research system, benchmark tasks designed by the authors, and dependence on commercial language models. It supports operational network flow analysis, digital twin interfaces and emergency decisions for gas pipelines, and could wrap simulators such as GasNetSim, which is catalogued here.
